author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Flycast enables translucent depth masking for Monkey Ball’s minimap
summary: Flycast’s arcade-specific boot settings now apply translucent polygon depth masking to Monkey Ball Japan Version as well as Cosmic Smash in Japan. The title-specific override targets the minimap rendering path without changing the global graphics default for other games.
heroAlt: Sega Dreamcast console with a controller and accessories.

blocks.text: A minimap can use a different depth rule

A game may draw its small map through a translucent polygon pass while the main scene uses ordinary depth testing. If that pass does not write or test depth the way the original arcade renderer expects, map layers can overlap incorrectly. The report for Monkey Ball Japan Version led to a focused configuration change, not a new general transparency algorithm.

Flycast already had a special arcade setting for Cosmic Smash in Japan that enabled translucent polygon depth masking. The merged fix extends that same condition to the product identifier `MONKEY BALL JAPAN VERSION`; it does not introduce a new renderer algorithm or a global default. The existing setting is applied at boot when Flycast recognizes the arcade platform.
Scope the behavior to the identified title

The change lives in the startup special-settings selection, where Flycast checks whether the loaded platform is an arcade system and then matches its product ID. That keeps the workaround attached to the game variant that needs it and avoids affecting unrelated Naomi or Dreamcast software, including other versions that may share an engine but not the same rendering behavior.
Verify both the intended map and other titles

The patch is small, but its correctness depends on the title identifier and the depth behavior of that game’s minimap pass. A useful check compares the map’s overlapping translucent layers in Monkey Ball Japan Version before and after the override, then confirms Cosmic Smash still receives its prior setting and other titles do not inherit it.
